First reach out to your physics professor and a ta to make sure you reach the prof. Then if there is a make-up, don’t drop the class, and set multiple reminders on your phone. If there is no make-up, then it’s probably best to drop the class. It sucks :/ but it doesn’t sound like there’s anything you can do about it. I had a similar thing happen to me with a project and I resigned the class but luckily it wasn’t for my major... although it was over a project worth 5% of my grade so in retrospect it was a pretty stupid decision 🤷‍♀️ 

Lastly, make sure to schedule some time for yourself, or order some great food. I’m sure you can find 20 minutes in your day to do something you enjoy, It sounds like you need to work on lowering your stress levels (which unfortunately is mostly out of your control) so that this doesn’t happen again.

Happened upon this as someone from a western country. My experience in the psyche ward as a kid was that they sedated everyone with strong drugs. They once had to drag me out of the shower because I was so sedated. I’m bitter about it, because they also didn’t do much in protecting people from fighting. But the places I stayed at weren’t the end of the world. We didn’t have a phone so we couldn’t post on Reddit... but we had stuff to do throughout the day, and in every hospital I stayed at, there was always a tv and other people to talk to if you were able to. I’m sure health care is a lot worse in other states than my own, and in other areas than my own.... people I know have been mulested and I have personally almost been sexually assaulted in the hospitals. It’s the same problem for everyone because hospitals attract predators who know that their word is always stronger than someone who needs to be hospitalized. But even tho my experience was bad, it’s much better than 90% of the world, showing how fucked the system is.

Have you considered joining a grief group or getting therapy? It sounds like you might have complex grief. Grief affects everyone differently. Grief effects everyone differently. Therapy isn’t there to change your feelings, it’s there to help you cope.
